title: f-Differential Privacy Filters: Validity and Approximate Solutions
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Naively composing trade-off curves under adaptivity gives a curve that differs from the true one, so the natural filter is invalid.
layout: 4 panels in a row, left-to-right, shared axes, colored curves with legends
description: Four side-by-side line plots share the same axes, with type II error f(α) on the y-axis and α from 0 to 1 on the x-axis. Panel (a) shows two trade-off functions: f21 is a smooth red convex curve, and f22 is a blue piecewise-linear curve that hits zero at α=0.5. Panel (b) shows the tensor products f1⊗f21 in red and f1⊗f22 in blue, plus a black curve f_B that follows the lower envelope of the two. Panel (c) compares f_B in black with the adaptive composition f1⊗_adapt f2^(y1) in magenta. The two curves cross, so the adaptive composition is not dominated by f_B. Panel (d) shows the symmetrized versions of both curves, with a sharp drop near α=0 and a linear middle section. The eye goes first to the colored curves in panel (a), then follows them across the panels. Each panel has a legend in the top right and a bold panel letter in the bottom left.
caption: Privacy filter in fully adaptive composition
abstract: Accounting for privacy loss under fully adaptive composition---where mechanism choice and privacy parameters may depend on the history of prior outputs---is a central challenge in differential privacy (DP). Here, privacy filters are stopping rules ensuring a prescribed global budget is not exceeded. A leading candidate for optimal filter design is $f$-DP, which characterizes the full extent of adversarial hypothesis testing and recovers $(\varepsilon,Î´)$-DP through piece-wise linear trade-off functions, while enabling tight $(\varepsilon,Î´)$-DP accounting in standard compositions via tensor products. Yet whether such filters can be correctly defined under $f$-DP remains unclear. We show that the natural $f$-DP filter---tracking path-wise accumulating tensor products and stopping when the prescribed curve is crossed---is fundamentally invalid, precluding the direct use of standard efficient numerical Fast-Fourier-Transform accounting in the fully adaptive setting. We characterize this failure, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for the natural filter's validity. Furthermore, we prove a fully adaptive central limit theorem for $f$-DP, establishing Gaussian convergence of cumulative privacy losses under full adaptivity. As a demonstration, we construct a closed-form approximate GDP filter for subsampled Gaussian mechanisms that provably outperforms RDP-based accounting in asymptotic regimes ($q\ll 1$ and $q\approx 1$) without tracking the full trade-off function, demonstrating that the slack in RDP is not intrinsic to adaptive composition---though CLT-based approximations are known to be optimistic at realistic subsampling rates, a limitation that remains an open challenge.
